name: Plant-fibre fabrics and cordage among early Andean foragers
summary: Direct dates from Guitarrero Cave in Peru document two-ply cord and both close- and open-twined plant-fibre textiles by the early Holocene.
description: Foragers in the Peruvian Andes made plant-fibre cord and twined fabrics. A directly dated fragment from Guitarrero Cave has tightly spaced twining and plied leaf-fibre yarns. A second fragment has more widely spaced twining and includes whole rushlike stems. Coils of processed fibres support the interpretation that some fibre work took place in the cave.

impact.note: Lowered from the lead's 2/2/2 because the origin is unknown and no descent from this community is shown: the finds witness fabric and rope making among early Andean foragers (reach 1), a basic capability for carrying, storing and bedding (depth 2), with later Andean fibre work as likely but unproven successors (generativity 1).

date.label: 12,130–11,080 cal BP across dated specimens
date.basis: The quoted interval spans the oldest and youngest boundaries of the early fibre determinations in Jolie et al. Table 2. Individual specimen intervals are separate.

events.statement: A two-ply cord dates to 12,130–11,800 cal BP. Closely and openly twined fragments date to 11,330–11,100 and 11,280–11,080 cal BP respectively.

evidence.supports: Direct determinations distinguish the early two-ply cord and close and open twining from a much later spiral-interlinked fragment.
The article describes the textile structures, constituent fibres and possible uses and reports fibre coils among the excavated material.

events.caveats: Direct dates apply to the sampled cords and fabrics. The tested spiral-interlinked fragment was much younger. Clothing, containers and matting are interpretations of fragment form and wear.

earliest_record.rationale: The sampled objects have direct AMS dates. The cord is older than the two dated twined fabrics.

unresolved.note: Close twining may have formed a bag or clothing. Open twining is interpreted as likely matting. No evidence links this assemblage directly to later Andean coastal twining.
The cave coordinates are shown in the registry as recalled and can be checked against a site survey.

research.note: The source now gives original artifact and radiocarbon tables rather than a press release. The different dates limit what can be inferred about contemporaneity of techniques.
